resolved: 2026-07-27, after measuring. Outcomes recorded in place -- predictions are not edited away.
why: The site currently recommends 'decode 看 INT4' as the headline. That is only right for generation-heavy workloads. For a VLM understanding task (long multimodal input, very short answer) prefill dominates, and weight-only INT4 gives nothing on prefill (INT4 prefill ~= FP16, see roofline 1.4) while INT8 gets 1.87x from native int8 cores. So there must be a crossover.

model.assumption: TTFT approximately linear in n_in over 128..1024; attention O(n^2) adds ~4% at 1024 and ~14% at 4096 so linearity understates TTFT at 4096

outcomes.measured: INT4 4.61 s vs INT8 6.87 s on goat = 1.49x
run_int4.log / run_int8.log inference phase 77.4 s vs 54.2 s over 110 requests = 703 vs 493 ms/request = 1.43x

outcomes.verdict: CONFIRMED -- the compute-bound model (62.0 TFLOP matmul + 9.9 TFLOP attention at 27.1 TFLOP/s effective) predicts long-input prefill to within 4%

outcomes.predicted: n_out = n_in / 65.3 (from the old engine pair at 512)
outcomes.measured_best_tuned: n_out = n_in / 66.5 (old int4 vs old int8 at 512, i.e. each precision at its best-tuned build)
outcomes.verdict: CONFIRMED in form, and the prediction matches the best-tuned pair almost exactly (65.3 vs 66.5). The matched-pair boundary sits at /83 only because the len4096 INT8 engine carries a ~15% prefill penalty (see opt_shape_finding), which works AGAINST INT8 -- so the 'INT8 wins on long-input/short-output' conclusion is conservative either way.

outcomes.predicted: unchanged -- maxInputLen sizes activations/profile, not weights
outcomes.measured: INT4 5.7 G at both 1024 and 4096; INT8 8.9 G at both; visual 1.1 G despite maxImageTokens 1024->4096

opt_shape_finding.what: llmBuilder.cpp sets the TRT optimization profile to opt = maxInputLen/2, max = maxInputLen (variable names optCtxShape / maxCtxShape). Raising maxInputLen therefore moves the tuning point.
opt_shape_finding.result: INT4 is unaffected (<=0.5% at every length). INT8 pays +15.3% at 512 and +15.5% at 1024, and nothing at 128.
opt_shape_finding.caveat_resolved: The len4096 engines changed THREE things at once, so two single-variable control builds were run to attribute the penalty.

attribution.maxBatchSize 4->1: +6.0% / +6.7% => real, and counter-intuitive: shrinking the profile's max batch makes batch-1 prefill SLOWER. TRT tunes tactics for opt=(maxBatchSize, maxInputLen/2); the batch-4 opt apparently selects kernels that also serve batch 1 better.
attribution.total: ~+15%, and the two causes are independent and roughly additive

opt_shape_finding.why_int8_only: INT4 is W4A16 -- weights are dequantized and the GEMM runs in fp16, a path whose tactic choice is shape-insensitive here. INT8 is W8A8 on native int8 tensor cores, where the tactic/tile space is richer and more shape-sensitive. Mechanism is inferred, not proven.
opt_shape_finding.practical_consequence: On this 32 GB device INT8 cannot have both: maxInputLen 4096 with maxBatchSize 4 would very likely exceed the build-memory ceiling, and dropping to batch 1 costs 6%. So INT8's capacity upgrade costs ~15% prefill, of which 6% is forced. INT4 pays nothing at all. Even so INT8 is still 1.57x faster than INT4 at 4096 input (1625.6 vs 2554.6 ms) -- without the penalty it would be ~1.82x.

int8_len4096.note: 29.7 GB on a ~30 GB machine -- essentially at the ceiling.
int8_len4096.claim_retracted: I first wrote that maxBatchSize 4->1 was *required* because a batch-4 profile would be 4x larger and would have OOM'd. The control builds disprove that: int8_ctl_b1 (len1024, batch1) already peaked at 29105 MB and int8_ctl_kv8k (len1024, batch4, KV8192) at 27571 MB, so going from len1024 to len4096 added only ~0.6 GB. INT8 build peak is ~28-30 GB regardless of these knobs -- it is dominated by the builder's weight workspace, not by the activation profile. Batch 4 at len 4096 might well have fit. Untested.

decode_200_iter.why: published TPOT rested on 10 iterations with std 6.89 ms (20% of the mean), so the +-13% CI was wider than the reported precision
decode_200_iter.note: decode is unaffected by the opt shift (its profile is seq=1). Published INT4 TPOT was 32.34 (dog) / 33.93 (repro); the 200-iteration value is 30.78, i.e. 4.8-9.3% lower -- the old 10-iteration numbers were noise-inflated.

lm_head_quantization_v7_v8.v7_2B_single_gpu: device_map={'':0} -> CUDA OOM, tried to allocate 4.64 GiB, GPU0 had 1.94 GiB free (process already 12.62 GiB for a 4.3 GiB model => quantize footprint is ~3x weights)
lm_head_quantization_v7_v8.v8_8B_asymmetric: max_memory={0:'13GiB',1:'7GiB'} -> placement {0:16, 1:19, disk:6}: 6 modules offloaded to DISK -> illegal memory access in AWQ calibration (same class as v4/v6)
both_hypotheses_refuted: 'asymmetric budget summing above the 16.34 GiB model prevents spill' -- WRONG: accelerate reserves extra per device, and the spill target was disk, not CPU
'2B fp16 is only 4.3 GiB so a single T4 is trivially safe' -- WRONG: the quantize process peaks at ~3x the weights
lm_head_quantization_v7_v8.mechanism_finally_identified: 4.64 GiB factorises exactly as calib_batch 16 x seq 512 x vocab 151936 x 4 B (fp32) => quantizing lm_head materialises the full LOGITS tensor for the calibration batch. Its size is set by batch x seq x vocab and is INDEPENDENT of weight size -- which is why switching 8B->2B does not help at all (same vocab 151936, same logits tensor).
lm_head_quantization_v7_v8.contrast: 8B's earlier v3/v5 OOM asked for 1.16 GiB = 4096 x 151936 x 2 B, i.e. the lm_head WEIGHT -- a different tensor. Both are fatal, by different mechanisms.
lm_head_quantization_v7_v8.new_cheapest_fix: drop the AWQ calibration batch from 16 to 1-2 (the documented default is AWQ=16): logits tensor shrinks 8-16x, 4.64 GiB -> 0.29 GiB. Cheaper than waiting for a >=24 GB GPU and should be tried first.
lm_head_quantization_v7_v8.status: +19~23% decode gain remains an UNVERIFIED PREDICTION (7 attempts, 0 successes)

Batch 1 shrinks it 16x to 0.29 GiB. The first 8 attempts all searched the wrong axes (total VRAM, module placement); once the right axis was identified, attempt 9 passed both models on the first try.

lm_head_quantization_v9_SUCCESS.cost: 190 min wall (vs 9-15 min for each failure) -- batch 16->1 makes calibration ~12x slower over the same 512 samples
lm_head_quantization_v9_SUCCESS.CAVEAT_calibration_config_changed: calib batch affects AWQ per-channel scale estimation, so the batch=1 model is NOT the same quantization config as the deployed batch=16 INT4. num_samples stays 512 so coverage is unchanged, but 'accumulated one-by-one' vs 'parallel within batch' differs.
lm_head_quantization_v9_SUCCESS.still_unverified: +19~23% decode gain. Remaining steps: pull artifact -> Orin llm_build -> llm_bench decode -> AND n=210 accuracy, reported alongside the batch=16 INT4. Reporting speed without accuracy would be claiming a win for a model whose recipe changed.
